briefdescription.para: Analyze the branch statement to determine if it can be coalesced.

detaileddescription.para:
This method analyses the branch statement for the given candidate to determine if it can be coalesced. If the branch can be coalesced, then the BranchTargetBlock and the FallThroughBlock are recorded in the specified Candidate.

true if and only if the branch can be coalesced, false otherwise

briefdescription.para: Merge the instructions from SourceRegion.BranchBlock, SourceRegion.BranchTargetBlock, and SourceRegion.FallThroughBlock into TargetRegion.BranchBlock, TargetRegion.BranchTargetBlock and TargetRegion.FallThroughBlock respectively.

detaileddescription.para: The successors for blocks in TargetRegion will be updated to use the successors from blocks in SourceRegion. Finally, the blocks in SourceRegion will be removed from the function.

A region consists of a BranchBlock, a FallThroughBlock, and a BranchTargetBlock. Branch coalesce works on patterns where the TargetRegion's BranchTargetBlock must also be the SourceRegions's BranchBlock.

briefdescription.para: This function checks if MI can be moved to the end of the TargetMBB, immediately before the first terminator.

detaileddescription.para: A MI instruction can be moved to then end of the TargetMBB if no PHI node defines what MI uses within it's own MBB.

parameterdescription.para: the machine basic block to move to

simplesect.para: true if it is safe to move MI to end of TargetMBB, false otherwise.

briefdescription.para: This method determines whether the two coalescing candidates can be merged.

detaileddescription.para: This function first try to move instructions from the TargetRegion.BranchTargetBlock down, to the beginning of the SourceRegion.BranchTargetBlock. This is not possible if any register defined in TargetRegion.BranchTargetBlock is used in a PHI node in the SourceRegion.BranchTargetBlock. In this case, check whether the statement can be moved up, to the end of the TargetRegion.BranchBlock (immediately before the branch statement). If it cannot move, then these blocks cannot be merged.
Note that there is no analysis for moving instructions past the fall-through blocks because they are confirmed to be empty. An assert is thrown if they are not.
